question: Provision of 'First Past the Post' in Indian Constitution has been adopted from the constitution of:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Britain**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The provision of 'First Past the Post' (**FPTP**) in the Indian Constitution has been adopted from the Constitution of the United Kingdom.
 
• This electoral system is used for electing **members of the Lok Sabha **(House of the People) and **state legislative assemblies** in India.
 
• The system is **straightforward for voters to understand** and for officials to administer. Election results can be counted and announced relatively **quickly **compared to more complex voting systems.
 
• **How FPTP Works**
 
 
• Each electoral constituency elects one representative.
 
• Voters cast their vote for their preferred candidate. In FPTP, voters typically mark their choice for one candidate only.
 
• The candidate who receives the most votes in that constituency wins. Importantly, they do not need to secure an absolute majority (more than 50% of the votes); they just need to have more votes than any other candidate.
